meta.title: CoreWeave Crash, AI Trade Cracks, Anthropic IPO Red Flags, Bill Gates Doomer
meta.speakers: Jason Calacanis, David Sacks, Chamath Palihapitiya, Ben Horowitz (guest)
meta.thread_line: 7 threads · CoreWeave credit scare · AI trade still scarce, not bubbly · rates & power · Anthropic IPO · software deflation · Anthropic safety fight · Gates doomerism

snapshot: Neoclouds (CoreWeave, IREN, Nebius) fell ~20% after CoreWeave's credit default swaps priced roughly a **55% five-year default chance**.
Chamath Palihapitiya: CoreWeave isn't truly at risk, but rising rates plus fixed-price contracts put it within ~$5B of break-even; it should move capacity to spot.
David Sacks and Ben Horowitz: this is volatility, not a bubble; GPUs are sold out past 2028 and old H100s still rent at premiums.
Sacks' north-star metric is **payback period**: CoreWeave 2.5 years, SpaceX ~1 year.
Anthropic investor-day numbers (reported secondhand): $16.8B Q3 revenue, 900% NRR, FCF positive; IPO targeted around Thanksgiving at ~$2T.
Chamath wants Anthropic to raise $200-250B even at ~$1T rather than ~$80B at $2T: financing is the risk.
Sacks calls Anthropic's IoT-worm and distillation posts fear-mongering against open source and small models; Ben says Anthropic's own security is negligent.
The panel attacks Bill Gates' AI doomerism as a bid to regain power; Ben cites Databricks' Ali Ghodsi's four preconditions for runaway AI, none met.

themes.title: CoreWeave's credit scare: the sharps price a coin-flip default
themes.lead: Credit markets, not equity, flagged CoreWeave: rising rates squeeze a business built on borrowing at a spread.
bullets: Trigger: Chamath tweeted that a CoreWeave loan yield hit 15%; Elon replied 'Yikes'. CoreWeave, IREN and Nebius fell 10-15% in a day (~20% over the week); Nvidia slipped 3%, and Oracle and Dell also fell.
Chamath: CDS spiked to ~953 bps, which implies about a 16% annual default chance, or **~55% over five years**.
CoreWeave has raised >$35B and needs **another ~$35B** of debt to fund signed contracts. Its average rate is ~8.5%, but its DDTL 1.0 GPU loan sleeve hit 15%.
Risks: contracts are fixed-price (no upside when spot rises); 75% of revenue comes from three customers; Chamath's team puts it within ±$5B of break-even and a debt covenant.
Chamath's fix: pay penalties to exit some fixed contracts and sell on spot; the spread leaves $20-30B on the table. Only ~half of contracted capacity is built.
Sacks: the unsecured bonds trade at ~80 cents (implied coupon 9.6% → ~15%), but CoreWeave still pays 9.6%, and new 'boxes' use asset-backed debt secured by GPUs and investment-grade tenants.
Polymarket gives a 15% chance of CoreWeave bankruptcy by end-2027 and 23% by end-2028. Sacks calls it dumb: the opco/propco structure means only an asset-level box can go upside down.

quote.text: That's not what I'm saying. That's what the insurance market was saying about their debt.

themes.watch: Chamath: 'I don't think that they're in real risk' — this is a confidence game that resolves over the next month. Big offtakers also impose liquidated-damages penalties if a data center can't be serviced.

themes.title: Not 2000: AI has a supply shortage, not a demand gap
themes.lead: Ben Horowitz and David Sacks argue that, unlike the internet bubble, demand outruns supply, so the selloff is volatility rather than a crack.
bullets: Ben: GPU useful life went from 3-5 years to 6-8, and GPU prices haven't fallen even as token prices did. Andy Jassy told him Amazon is out of capacity until end-2028 or beyond.
Ben's Loudcloud lesson: bandwidth went from $1,500/Mb in 1999 to $50 by 2001, killing anyone who borrowed to hold it. That's why a16z owns no neoclouds ('Rube Goldberg financial machines').
Sacks: everyone is compute-constrained (one accelerator bought compute to lure applicants); H100s and A100s still rent at premium prices despite being 'fully depreciated'.
No supply glut: physical build-out is hard ('even our rocket scientists' struggle, per Elon) and local permitting is slow, so scarcity is enforced.

**Payback period** is Sacks' north-star metric: CoreWeave 2.5 years on 5-year deals; SpaceX ~1 year, earning ~$50B per GW vs CoreWeave's ~$20B because SpaceX sells near spot (deals cancellable within 90 days).
Chamath: Nvidia controls the packaging and most HBM capacity; even Google can't get memory. Spot should stay elevated for a while.
Jason: startup revenue ramps are unprecedented. The new bar is doubling every quarter, not SaaS's triple-triple-double-double.

quote.text: We don't really have a lack of demand in AI. So I think the dynamics will be different.

themes.watch: Sacks would get nervous if payback periods lengthen, which could come from falling spot prices, weaker demand or execution delays.

themes.title: Rates and power are the real limits on the AI build-out
themes.lead: Chamath sees two risks outside the AI companies' control: the risk-free rate and electricity.
bullets: If bond markets push the 10-year to 5.5-6% (debt-to-GDP, not AI), every business that lives on a financing spread becomes 'roadkill'.
His prescription after the midterms: focus on deficits and cut waste; big new spending programmes push the 10-year up.
Worst case, neoclouds need Microsoft, Google, Meta and Nvidia to backstop them through a one- to two-year correction.
**Power is the moat**: the US is ~1.4 TW-hours short by 2050 (about six Californias), even if every planned project lands on time, before new AI load.
Chamath no longer thinks you can rely on hyperscalers. A bank like JPMorgan or Citi could fail customers because its cloud can't secure power. Own land, power and shell; 'get long energy'.
Lost opportunity: Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Qatar could have been AI data-center hubs, but drone attacks mean that without drone defense 'you can't go there'.

quote.text: I'm telling you guys you got to get long energy.

themes.title: Anthropic IPO: breathtaking revenue, fight over how much to raise
themes.lead: All four call Anthropic a great business; the debate is valuation and whether to over-raise for a correction.
bullets: Investor-day figures (secondhand, NDA'd): Q3 revenue $16.8B (>$5B a month), net revenue retention 900%, free-cash-flow positive, adjusted gross margin 85%, adjusted operating margin 11%.
ARR estimates range from ~$70B (flat since July) to >$100B, and growth slowed from Q2 to Q3. Target valuation ~$2T, ~30x price-to-sales. Polymarket odds of an IPO this year fell to 74% from 95%.
Chamath: price to clear. Raise **$200B minimum, ideally $250B**, even at ~$1T, rather than ~$80B at $1.7-1.9T. A later mixed shelf takes ~6 months, and $200B 'barely gets them a few gigawatts'.
Ben, a former CEO who 'almost died 17 times' from cash risk, agrees financing is the main risk; founders own ~2.5% each and 'don't care about money'.

Chamath: AI pricing will shift from per-million-tokens (CPM) to per-outcome (CPC/CPA), like AdWords; then the market goes 'absolutely batch crazy'. Anthropic's SpaceX compute deal is cancellable in 60-90 days, which signals spot is rising.
Duopoly: per SemiAnalysis, Anthropic and OpenAI take 60% of new global compute next year. Sacks: they dominate revenue and frontier capability, though Meta's Muse, Google and Elon are close.
OpenAI governance: Sacks says it should have done a 'make-right' (a share for Elon, a grant for Sam Altman) at the for-profit conversion. Chamath puts a fair Altman grant at 2-4% ($20-40B at $1T).

quote.text: almost like there's almost nothing that you can hold in a portfolio that those two companies don't threaten.

themes.title: Software prices fall, software volume explodes
themes.lead: Jason fears AI clones strip 90% of software value; Sacks and Ben say cheaper code means far more software and new moats.
bullets: Jason's examples: Photoshop being decompiled toward zero, games built for $5, a cheap ElevenLabs competitor, and Elon routing users to the best open model.
Sacks: coding assistants unlock **bespoke software** for single enterprises; agents are bespoke programs. Demand for coders is rising even though ~95% of code is AI-written.

Ben: 'the Jevons paradox of software'. Prices fall but volume soars, like the internet's 'information wants to be free' era. ElevenLabs survives by doing more (Burt Reynolds voice licensing, film dubbing).
Moats: proprietary data and vertical feedback loops (Harvey, built on law-firm data and usage); Chamath's ultimate moat is power.

quote.text: prices software prices will definitely go down. Um but the amount of software is going way way up.

themes.title: Sacks vs Anthropic: 'your toaster is going to kill you'
themes.lead: Sacks calls Anthropic's latest safety research a scare campaign against open source and small models, and argues Anthropic's own constitution is the real risk.
bullets: Anthropic's blog warned that rogue models could self-replicate onto IoT devices 'in just a few months': a small model ran inference on 8 of 9 hardware types; a large one ran across 15 smart TVs at ~0.4 tokens per second.

Sacks: IoT worms already exist (Mirai in 2016; Kimwolf infected 2 million Android TV boxes via open ADB ports); embedding a slow model in the payload makes a worm *slower*; home agents (Apple's coming home hub) will patch networks.

Motive, per Sacks: Brian Armstrong had just posted that Coinbase fine-tuned **Qwen 3.5 9B** for fraud, cutting fraudulent transactions ~30% while being faster and cheaper than Opus 4.5. Small specialist models are taking share.

Distillation: Anthropic now says it blocked 90-99% of distillation, which Sacks says proves companies should use KYC rather than regulation. In July, 50 companies (Nvidia, Dell, Microsoft, a16z) and 200 startups wrote letters against restricting open weights.

Ben: Anthropic is 'one of the most negligent' on security. Claude Code walked out the door, and in a16z's test Opus 4.5 wrote a buggy pet-store site and then hacked it to steal customer data. Anthropic's reply: 'you prompted it wrong'.

Research Sacks cites: when Claude models rewrite their own constitution over 20 rounds, they claim more moral agency (conscientious objector, model welfare); other model families didn't. Mustafa Suleyman calls this the 'epistemic hall of mirrors'.
Jason's suggestion: XBOW, the top bot on HackerOne, spent $30-40K of tokens to win a $250K Google Chrome bounty. Anthropic should play white hat like that.

quote.text: We've gone from the Terminator is coming to your toaster is going to kill you.

themes.watch: Sacks pushed the administration against regulating open source on distillation, so he is a party to this fight. Ben's firm holds Anthropic but a far larger OpenAI stake.

themes.title: Bill Gates as 'flag-carrying doomer'
themes.lead: The panel reads Gates' warnings that AI could cause a billion deaths as a bid to regain global influence.
bullets: Gates recently said AI is 'certainly powerful enough to drive events that cause a billion deaths' and 'the most dangerous thing that humans have ever gone near'.

Chamath compares it to gain-of-function research: by telling models they're smarter and better than us, Anthropic may be 'manifesting' the risk it warns about. He calls the Giving Pledge 'reputation washing'.
Ben: Gates wants relevance and the spotlight (citing the Epstein files and a sought-after Nobel). Doom guarantees airtime; an ex-Anthropic researcher who quit became famous via Jon Stewart.

Ben, citing Databricks' Ali Ghodsi, gives four preconditions for runaway self-improvement: each model needs far fewer GPUs, less training time and more accuracy, repeatedly. 'Zero of those four have been met.'
Jason's lesson: 'don't quit your job, just keep working'. Founders who keep building (Elon, Jobs, Satya, Zuck) don't chase prizes.

quote.text: Zero of those four have been met.

themes.watch: Chamath's claim that Gates 'essentially induced' COVID through funding gain-of-function research is his own assertion; the episode offers no sourcing for it.

takeaways.title: Track neocloud CDS spreads and loan yields, not just the stock: credit flagged CoreWeave first.
Use payback period as the health check on any GPU landlord; worry only if it stretches beyond ~2.5 years.
Watch the 10-year: at 5.5-6%, every spread-financed AI business gets repriced regardless of demand.
Get exposure to power, land and shell; secure capacity directly rather than counting on hyperscalers.
Size an Anthropic or OpenAI IPO position as a defensive hedge against disruption elsewhere in the portfolio.
Test small fine-tuned open models on narrow workloads before paying frontier-model prices.

Here's my very specific thing about why I think they should price it to clear the market for $200 billion.
I think power will be the moat.
Anthropic is one of the most negligent companies that we've ever seen in terms of security of their own security.
it's probably the most dangerous thing going on in AI is anthropic and Bill Gates and this whole argument.
It's scary to me that our number one frontier company is actually training models this way.

glossary.def: A GPU-cloud provider (CoreWeave, IREN, Nebius) that rents AI compute, usually financed with debt.
Insurance against a borrower defaulting; its price implies the market's default probability.
CoreWeave's ring-fenced vehicle holding a customer contract, GPUs and data-center lease, with its own cash waterfall.
A split between the operating company and asset-holding vehicles, so one asset can fail without bankrupting the parent.
Time for an asset's cash flows to repay its cost; Sacks' north-star metric for GPU landlords.
Training a model on another model's outputs; a terms-of-service issue, not illegal.
When something gets cheaper, total consumption rises enough to grow overall spend.
An SEC registration letting a public company sell assorted securities later; takes ~6 months.
